full_judgment:
MOHAMMAD ISMAILUDDIN SARKER, J.: This petition by defendant No. 1 petitioner is against the judgment and decree dated August 30, 1994 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 271 of 1992 affirming the judgment and decree dated October 21, 1992 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Third Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.14 of 1980 decreeing the suit for specific performance of contract. 

 4. At the trial respondent No. 1 examined two witnesses including himself and produced certain documents which were marked exhibits. He examined one Matiur Rahman as P.W,2 who was supervisor of the B.C.C.I Bank , Motijheel Branch at the relevant time. P.W. 2 stated that the petitioner had an account with the aforesaid Bank in the- name of his firm Purbanchal Corporation bearing C.D. Account No. 1428 and in that account there was a balance of Tk. 260/- only on May 2, 1979 and also on May 15, 1979. The petitioner examined 4 witnesses including himself. As D.W. 1 he stated that he obtained permission from the Government for selling 10 kathas of land and applied for gain-tax clearance certificate but while he was trying to obtain gain-tax clearance certificate respondent No. 1 came to him and declared that he would not take the land as he would purchase piece of land in Gulshan and wanted the earnest money back by cancelling the agreement. The petitioner agreed to the proposal of respondent No. 1 and issued a cheque for an amount of Tk. 2,54,500/- on May 2, 1979 with a request to present the cheque within 2/3 days for encashment. The other three defence witnesses stated that they were present when respondent No. 1 came to the petitioner and asked to return the earnest money. On consideration of the evidence on record the learned Subordinate Judge decreed the suit. On appeal by the petitioner, the High Court Division after considering the evidence both the oral and documentary and the submissions made on behalf of the petitioner dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. The learned Judges further directed respondent No. 1 to pay the proportionate outstanding loan of respondent No. 4 and also directed respondent No. 4 to calculate the proportionate outstanding loan of 9 kathas of land out of 21 kathas and realise the same from respondent No. 1. 

 5. Dr. Rafiqur Rahman, the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner submitted that the contract having been mutually cancelled by issuing a cheque by the petitioner refunding the earnest money the non-encashment of the cheque might entail other consequences, but that cannot revive the terminated contract and as such the learned Judges of the High Court Division has committed an error of law in upholding the decree for specific performance of contract. It appears from the judgment of the High Court Division that when the petitioner issued the cheque on May 2, 1979 there was only a sum of Tk. 260/- in his account. Considering the evidence of P.W. 2 along with exhibits 9 and 9 (a) the High Court Division found that from January 1, 1979 the alleged Country Manager Mr. Nuruddin ceased to perform his function as Country Manager of the Bank as he was transferred elsewhere from Bangladesh. The learned Judges of the High Court Division further noticed that although the petitioner is a retired Army Officer he with a malafide intention to defeat the purpose of the agreement for sale of the suit land committed fraud upon the plaintiff-respondent by issuing a cheque upon a. concocted story of his alleged conversation with the Country Manager of the B.C.C.I. Bank. Although respondent No, 1 accepted the cheque from the petitioner in good faith he did not hand over the agreement to the petitioner and as the cheque was dishonored by the Bank, the agreement remained in force; and as such the suit for specific performance of contract was very much maintainable. Therefore, it cannot be said that the contract was mutually cancelled and the suit for specific performance of contract was not maintainable. Hence this petition is dismissed.
